themes_detail.label: Street noise explosion
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints spiked to 70 this week—a 575% jump from the 10.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 13.34)—suggesting a sudden, acute disruption affecting multiple blocks in Bed-Stuy.
evidence: 70 noise complaints this week vs. 10.4 weekly average (575% increase, z-score: 13.34)
Represents most acute single-week spike in complaint data
Statistically significant deviation indicating new or sudden event, not gradual trend
reporting_angles: Interview residents on affected blocks to identify source: construction, venue, transit, or other cause
Cross-reference with DOB permits and NYC Parks maintenance schedules filed in past 90 days (799 total filings suggest active work)

themes_detail.label: Abandoned bikes piling up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints hit 7 last week—a 1020% spike from the 0.6 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 13.17)—indicating a new dumping pattern or bike-share malfunction affecting public space.
evidence: 7 abandoned bike complaints last week vs. 0.6 weekly average (1020% increase, z-score: 13.17)
Near-zero baseline suggests this is an entirely new phenomenon, not seasonal fluctuation
Likely concentrated geographically; could indicate single hotspot
reporting_angles: Map the 7 complaints to identify geographic cluster and interview residents at those locations
Contact Citi Bike to determine if there is a maintenance or user behavior issue driving the spike

themes_detail.label: Animal waste complaints surge
themes_detail.summary: Unsanitary animal conditions on private property spiked to 5 complaints two weeks ago—a 1233% jump from the 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 9.55)—suggesting potential hoarding, neglect, or pest issues emerging in households.
evidence: 5 animal sanitation complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (1233% increase, z-score: 9.55)
Unusually high z-score indicates statistical anomaly, not random variation
Private property complaints suggest household-level issue, harder to detect than public space problems
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Health to learn if inspectors visited flagged addresses and what violations were found
Interview animal welfare advocates or veterinarians about whether Bed-Stuy has reported animal neglect patterns

themes_detail.label: Trash disposal crisis emerging
themes_detail.summary: Residential disposal complaints jumped to 18 last week—a 200% increase from the 6.0 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 7.24)—suggesting a sanitation pickup failure or illegal dumping surge.
evidence: 18 disposal complaints last week vs. 6.0 weekly average (200% increase, z-score: 7.24)
Convergence signal: unsanitary conditions (814 complaints, 90-day total) remains top issue, now accompanied by disposal spike
Coincides with street sign and lot condition complaints, suggesting neighborhood-wide maintenance lapse
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY to determine if there is a collection route failure or staffing issue in CD 303
Survey blocks with highest complaints to document pile-up and interview residents about frequency of service

themes_detail.label: Street infrastructure neglect
themes_detail.summary: Missing street signs (3 complaints last week, +2300% from 0.1 weekly average) and dead/dying trees (3 complaints 2 weeks ago, +2300%) indicate a wider municipal maintenance gap in Bed-Stuy's public realm.
evidence: Missing street signs: 3 complaints last week vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Dead/dying trees: 3 complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average (2300% increase, z-score: 8.69)
Community Board budget shows repeated requests for DPR funding and park amenities—chronic underfunding signal
reporting_angles: Investigate whether NYC Parks and DOT have staffing or budget constraints limiting maintenance in this district
Interview Community Board members about backlog of infrastructure requests and city responsiveness
